title: I expected the AI to be the hard part of building an AI game. Turns out getting players to finish battles is harder.
author: Birthday_Euphoric
selftext:
Been building an experiment called RapArena.

**The idea sounded simple:**

* Player A challenges Player B
* Both submit hidden roast material
* AI writes and performs the rap battle
* People vote on the winner

**What surprised me:**

Generating the battle actually worked fairly quickly.

The harder problem was player behavior.

**A lot of people would:**

* create a battle
* send the invite
* then the second player never finishes

**So now I’m experimenting with things that feel more like game design than AI:**

* showing partial progress
* reducing wait time perception
* making battle creation feel lower effort
* giving spectators a reason to care

Curious for people building AI games:

Do you have any hack into getting social games to gain certain critical mass of players?

The game is free to play here: [https://raparena.ai](https://raparena.ai)

comments.author: OurPillowGuy
comments.body:
If there was a low cost “hack” into attaining a critical mass of players, you would have solved gaming as a business. Building the software was never the hard part. User acquisition and retention is.

You need to play test the game with a bunch of people to make sure it is fun and sticky, and make choices and changes that increase retention and lower barriers to entry. Also, ask yourself if the gamers you are targeting are excited to play a game that is so obviously AI forward.

replies.author: Birthday_Euphoric
replies.body:
That's true. Hmmm, I think this "game" is a bit more of party game that is for anyone out there who want to have fun roasting their friends through AI generated rap. I am guessing it's not the normal game in that sense so it's not really for normal gamers. 

Maybe I need to think of it as a business but I'm having trouble for Player B to accept a challenge from Player A who bothered to submit burns on the website.

replies.author: Birthday_Euphoric
replies.body: Cool! Didn't know about it. Just took a look at it! I guess the key difference is the fact that for Raparena, you can just submit the roasts/burns (without thinking about the rhymes because the AI does it for you) and it's a bit more readily accessible via the web but this is a great reference!
